title: A session's repository, as the Git panel reads it
description: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/git. The Swift app answers this from `GitChanges.payload`; the shape is that payload, field for field, because `input/git-panel.js` reads it directly. It is a reading taken when the panel opens, never a subscription: three lock-free `git` invocations, and no cache beyond the answer.

GitFileKind.description: What happened to one file. `conflict` outranks the rest — an unmerged path is the one row a reader must not mistake for an ordinary edit — and a rename is named before an add or a delete because Git reports it as both.

GitFile.description: One row of `git status --porcelain=v2`, with the two diff counts joined onto it. `staged` and `unstaged` are the two halves of the XY code and are not exclusive: a file edited after being added is both.

from.description: Where a rename came from; null for every other kind.

additions.description: Lines added, from `git diff --numstat` and `--cached --numstat` summed. Null when there is no measurement rather than zero: an untracked file appears in neither diff, and a binary side of one is a dash. A count of nothing and nothing counted are different facts and the panel draws them differently.

deletions.description: Lines removed, on the same terms as `additions`. Once either side of a pair is unknowable both stay null rather than presenting half a measurement.

GitSnapshot.description: The branch line and the changed files, as of the moment the panel asked.

branch.description: `# branch.head`. Empty on a detached HEAD, where the panel falls back to the first eight characters of `head`.

head.description: `# branch.oid`, or empty on a repository with no commit yet, where Git says `(initial)`.

clean.description: No changed files. Sent rather than derived so the two ends cannot disagree about what an empty list means.

GitReply.description: The reply body. One key, because the Swift route wraps the snapshot and the page reads `data.git`.
